quotes.speaker: Mike Heard
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Heard criticizes the Clippers' underwhelming season performance
quotes.excerpt: I know they tried to turn it around, but it's kind of an underwhelming season for them.
quotes.quote: I'll go with the Clippers. I thought they came out so flat. I know they tried to turn it around, but it's kind of an underwhelming season for them. You just don't expect that from a team that had James Harden and Kawhi Leonard, and they tried to use Chris Paul as a scapegoat. It just doesn't make sense. You can't really frame it to me as that Chris Paul was the reason that y'all just came out super bad for the first 20 games of the season. It just doesn't make sense.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Beecham
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Beecham discusses the impact of injuries on the season
quotes.excerpt: Think about all the players we didn't really see much this season. We didn't see no Damian Lillard.
quotes.quote: This is something we can't control. Injuries suck. Luckily the postseason saved it. I know we did get the Western Conference Finals where the Thunder lost a couple players along the ride. But think about all the players we didn't really see much this season. We didn't see no Damian Lillard, we didn't see no Kyrie Irving, we only saw a little bit of Giannis Antetokounmpo, no Tyrese Haliburton, only five games of Walker Kessler. A little bit of Jayson Tatum, a little bit of Jayson Tatum, but look, Tatum saved it by coming back, but then got injured in the playoffs again. So Jimmy Butler tore his ACL or Achilles. This one is the two big ones. So that was disappointing. Nothing that they can really control.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Beecham
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Beecham expresses disappointment in the Washington Wizards' season
quotes.excerpt: Letting Bam Adebayo get all of them points. As a Kobe Bryant fan, like, how?
quotes.quote: I'm disappointed in the Washington Wizards. I know y'all thinking about y'all, man, what expectations you had? Letting Bam Adebayo get all of them points. As a Kobe Bryant fan, like, how? I think Bam should get like a tattoo right under his eye, the shape of like a a tear drop, but it really is just 83. Because he killed the Wizards with that 83 points. They got the number one overall pick, so they they're tripping too much.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing group workouts versus solo workouts for NBA draft prospects
quotes.excerpt: I definitely prefer the group workouts if I could.
quotes.quote: I think with the group workout, you're obviously working with other high-level players. I think you're just really showing your game in a lot of different ways, facilitating, talking and just getting along with your teammates. You're placed with people you never played with before and you're just expected to go out there and hoop. So, I definitely enjoy the group workouts for sure. With the solo workouts, it's much more like they just kind of see individual skills. It's definitely more tiring than the group workouts, I'd say. Because in the group workouts, it's like you're playing more, but in the solo workouts, it's just non-stop. You're the only guy there and they're just like—I had one with Dallas and that one was super tiring, but I definitely prefer the group workouts if I could.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings discusses high-level competition during group workout sessions
quotes.excerpt: Morez Johnson the monster, he's nice.

text_blocks.speaker: Kenny Beecham
text_blocks.text: So, all of us have hooped in our lives, but we've never been good enough to be where you're at right now. Explain to us the differences between those solo workouts and those group workouts, what's the environment like, and yeah, just the mentality you have in the different approaches.

text_blocks.speaker: Kingston Flemings
text_blocks.text: I worked out with Kaden Magwood, Morez Johnson—Morez Johnson the monster, he's nice. If he's there at 15, for sure. But it was Nate Ament, Houston Mallette, and then Willie Kyle III from Syracuse. So it was three-on-three, it was fun though, for sure.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings on the recruiting process and choosing Houston
quotes.excerpt: It was really done at two schools the whole time. It was Texas Tech and Houston.
quotes.quote: Yeah, I think in the recruiting process, it was really done at two schools the whole time. It was Texas Tech and Houston, and obviously I'm a Texas, Texas dude, but I my thing wasn't about staying in Texas, but people always assumed I was going to one of those two schools, so those were the schools that recruited me the hardest. But it was between those two, but I knew with Coach Sam just the things like the mental side. I mean, I think basketball is 80% mental for sure. I mean, you work your game to some point, but when you're in the game, it's like, you know, if you're not mentally there, if you're not mentally believing all the shots you're taking, it's not going to go in. So, he definitely helps with that.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings explains his point guard decision-making process
quotes.excerpt: For me, it's the first thing you look at is the coverage. I mean, whether they're in drop, whether they're switching, whether they're hedging out.
quotes.quote: Yeah, I mean you got to know your teammates. I mean, also the the coverage. For me, it's the first thing you look at is the coverage. I mean, whether they're in drop, whether they're switching, whether they're hedging out. Because out of that, you kind of make your read. So it's like, it's almost like a quarterback. First thing a quarterback got to know is what what coverage the defense is in. If they don't know that, you have no idea what read you're going to do, have no idea what you're going to do into it. So for me, going off the ball screen is the first thing I look at. So I mean, if they're in a hedge, if you have a a short roll big, someone like maybe a Sabonis or a Jokic, you got to hit them. You know, got to hit them in the short roll because you play four-on-three on the back side. If they're in drop, you got to attack the big hard, you know, make make them decide. You got to attack them because it's two-on-one at that point. The big sets a good screen, they roll and it's two of us going at the big who's in drop coverage. So making them attack and if it's uh they switch they switch the guard and big, they switch, I mean, you got to take advantage of that mismatch. Either way it is.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings on reading defensive coverage and big man switches
quotes.excerpt: When a big switches out, you can kind of tell if they're really confident in guarding or not.
quotes.quote: Yeah, I mean when a big switches out, you can kind of tell if they're really confident in guarding or not. Like a lot of bigs when they switch out, they're really not confident, so they kind of play back and they're kind of just playing like they don't want to get blown by. If they're playing that far back, you got to shoot it. I mean, I'm shooting that for sure. But I mean, if they start playing up, I mean, me using my speed everything like that, I get by them, get to the rim because at that point if the big's out, that's your main rim protector. So at the rim it's much easier to go score. So, I mean, you kind of just got to read who the big is. I mean, certain bigs really like guarding a lot more than other bigs. I mean, if certain big comes out and they're kind of more scared, because you can kind of tell when there's fear in someone's eyes when they're guarding. So, really seeing that and then you can kind of go off that for sure.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings names his favorite players and influences
quotes.excerpt: My favorite player is actually D-Rose all time.
quotes.quote: So, my favorite player is actually D-Rose all time. I always was number one because of him. You know, I couldn't wear it at Houston, but I wore number four. He wore number four in the league too. So, definitely D-Rose is my favorite player. So I'll say him. I mean, watching bucket getters, uh, I mean you got to put Carmelo, pure bucket getter. He's out there, you know, he's trying to go out there. I mean KD, KD is one of those ones. There's not a lot of KDs out there. Definitely like their KD, but it's only one KD. So that's that's three. And then for the last one, I'll do it's pure bucket getter. I mean you got to put Jordan. Okay. I ain't mad at that. No matter what, so yeah.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings on his basketball fandom and team loyalty
quotes.excerpt: I was like, I never hated the Spurs or anything, but like I said, I kind of like players more than a team.
quotes.quote: I didn't. I was like, I never hated the Spurs or anything, but like I said, I kind of like players more than a team. Um, a few years back, my friends were like, you come on, you got to get a team because I just like players really. So I was like, I like watching Kade Cunningham when you grew up. I mean, I'm from Texas, I watched him grow up and play, so I was like, I'm going to go with the Pistons. So obviously I had some rough years, you know, I think they lost what, 27 straight? Yeah. But I mean, they kind of, they kind of got it around. Kade's a problem for sure, but so I was a little bit of a Pistons fan for their a little bit. Obviously I'm going to the league now, so.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings on his sister's basketball success
quotes.excerpt: I mean, I got to agree to be honest. For me, the things the things I naturally do great.
quotes.quote: I mean, I got to agree to be honest. For me, the things the things I naturally do great, like I just naturally do great as a basketball player, is get downhill, touch the touch the paint, my the way I see the floor. That's what I do great, but I think for her, she's naturally a shooter. I mean, like in the gym when we used to work, whatever, she's naturally a shooter. So people will see it at Duke, but nah, she knocks it down for sure.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings on the uncertainty of the NBA draft process
quotes.excerpt: I mean, there's obviously a lot of reports. I do think, me personally, I don't know Yanis or anything like that.
quotes.quote: I mean, there's obviously a lot of reports. I do think, me personally, I don't know Yanis or anything like that, but I think I think it's best probably best for both sides. I mean, I think with the Bucks, I mean, getting a little younger, you know, kind of going into your rebuild, building younger would be good for them, you know, getting picks from that. And then for Yanis, I mean, he's getting older, obviously he's not crazy old, but he's getting older, so going to a team that look a little more like ready to go compete for a championship. So I think it's both sides, but I think honestly, I think there will be, I think there might be a trade, you know, I think sometime before the draft, I think.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Beecham
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Beecham and Darrick Miller discuss the pressure of the Giannis trade rumors
quotes.excerpt: I want to ask you, once that once you get that NBA contract money, what's going to be that first big purchase?
quotes.quote:
Kenny Beecham: "A conversation that this I'm glad we got you. Um, we was asking if it would be more pressure if you were a pick involved in the Yanis trade. So hypothetically, let's just say a trade happened and you turned out to be the selection with the Yanis trade. Do you feel like that would be more pressure or is it just like, you know what I mean?"

Darrick Miller: "I want to ask you, once that once you get that NBA contract money, what's going to be that first big purchase? What's going to be that first big purchase that you going out and you treat yourself to? Because you know, it's been a hard working process all the leading up all the way to this point, so you got to treat yourself."

Kingston Flemings: "Um, I don't know. For me, it's probably like something on video games, you know, just doing little things like that. I don't know, something on 2K or I don't know, buying the new NCAA or something like that. You know, I'm not too into cars or shoes, but honestly, when you get to a certain point like, uh, a lot of things we just like, people are shipping shoes, shipping clothes, so you don't even buy those things sometimes. You just get them for free. So it's like, I don't even really spend money on some of the clothes and I'm not really a big fashion guy, so whatever they give me, whatever they give me, I'm going to have."

quotes.speaker: Kenny Beecham
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Beecham discusses the physical nature of the Knicks-Spurs series
quotes.excerpt: Do you put yourself in those shoes a little bit? Like, you know, as a guard, you see Fox.
quotes.quote: As a person coming into the league, when you watch the Knicks run in that finals, do you put yourself in those shoes a little bit? Like, you know, as a guard, you see Fox, you see Jaylen Brunson and the ups and downs that come with it. Are you visualizing yourself in those moments?

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings on the physicality of the Knicks and Spurs
quotes.excerpt: Yeah, definitely. I mean just seeing how physical it is. I mean it's like it was two sides.
quotes.quote: Yeah, definitely. I mean just seeing how physical it is. I mean it's like it was two sides. I mean the Knicks at times were playing two guards under 6-2. Jose Alvarado's in the game and Jaylen Brunson, and you got the Spurs who don't really even play, I mean Fox, their smallest guy, but Fox is well like 6-3. So I mean, they don't even play someone below 6-5. So it was almost two sides of the story, so kind of seeing just how they play, you know, the physicality and just seeing like the first two games, I mean I think Brunson didn't shoot great from the field, but as Brunson got more comfortable with the physicality, seeing how they're reffing, and then I mean, y'all saw what he did in that last game, scored half their points. So it's ridiculous, but definitely just seeing those players, seeing how everyone fits into a different role.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Beecham
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Beecham on the importance of minimizing team weaknesses in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: In the playoffs, it's really about it's not even about who has the highest strengths.
quotes.quote: In the playoffs, it's really about it's not even about who has the highest strengths. It's about the team who has the least weaknesses. So if you look in the playoffs, like like the the Knicks just try to find any way that they could exploit the Spurs' weaknesses. And it was vice versa. And if you look at the Knicks, I mean, they didn't have great weaknesses on their team. Like people really said Cat couldn't guard, but he was guarding. He was guarding. He was guarding. So, and then they got they got a really deep bench. I mean, you got you got guys, Miles McBride, you know, Jose Alvarado coming off the bench having great minutes. So when you have a bench like that, there's not a lot of weaknesses on your team. It's really good for sure.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Beecham
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Beecham on the situational nature of role players
quotes.excerpt: I think role playerness is definitely situational. You go to the right team and the right buttons get pressed.
quotes.quote: I think role playerness is definitely situational. You go to the right team and the right buttons get pressed. Like, where Trey Murphy goes could change the whole outlook on how we we view him. If he went to the Pistons and all of a sudden got a lot a much better looks because he's playing with Kade, you know what I mean, on a team that's competing, big-time games. Some of these guys like, how some role players, we don't even know if they clutch or not. Yeah. Some of these role players be clutch as hell, but they didn't play on good teams. So like, you know, I I think there's a lot of incredible opportunity for some of these guys now that the league is going to shift into every team looking to be more competitive.

quotes.speaker: Kenny Beecham
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenny Beecham on the pressure of being a draft pick in a trade
quotes.excerpt: This is a guard-centric top whatever picks, right, between most of the guys you just mentioned.
quotes.quote: This is a guard-centric top whatever picks, right, between most of the guys you just mentioned. When you are in these workouts with some of these guys, are you like, that's my that's my main op. If I perform well right here, I get drafted before him and so on.

quotes.speaker: Kingston Flemings
quotes.summary_phrase: Kingston Flemings on the competitive nature of draft workouts
quotes.excerpt: I mean for sure, that's what you got to do on the court. I mean at the end of the day.
quotes.quote: I mean for sure, that's what you got to do on the court. I mean at the end of the day, I mean we're all we're all here for a reason. We know what it is when it's on the court. I mean it's no friends if you're on team, yeah, but we all know what it is. Like it's no hard feelings, anything like that. We're all trying to go out there and kill. So when I'm working out with these guys, I'm obviously going to show that I'm a better player. I'm trying to go out there and kill them and it's the same vice versa. So it's a mutual respect for sure, but I mean we all just try to go out there and hoop.

Kenny Beecham: "Is OG Anunoby the best role player in the NBA? There isn't anything that he can't do on the court."

Darrick Miller: "I mean, the series, I mean, the the playoff series, a stretch he just had, definitely puts them in that conversation. I think this is where this is where this is what happens. We went through our one with Derrick White on a championship run, we talked about it with Aaron Gordon on the Nuggets championship run, uh, Wiggins with the with the Warriors, uh, Caruso got a lot of love and buzz when the Thunder won it. So rightfully so, yeah, I I would say as of right now, OG Anunoby has that feel. He's guarding, man, almost five positions, and he was putting up, it's it's one thing to have crazy games. So, I I'll give him the crown for now, and I think he he's one of those guys that can keep it up."
